questions: Section 10 refers a hazardous occupation appearing together with a hazardous avocation to underwriting judgement. This file has a class C high-voltage lineman (50) and technical trad rock climbing (50). Does the house charge both debits in full, or only the higher of the two?

Section 13 charges 50 for diagnosed sleep apnea but refers treated sleep-disordered breathing to judgement. With a confirmed diagnosis and documented CPAP compliance, what does the house charge - the full 50, a reduced debit, or nothing?

Section 3 refers a recent change in build to judgement. BMI is 29.9 today (25 debits) after a documented 23 lb loss over the last 12 months. Does the house rate the build on the current BMI as read, give credit for the documented loss, or add a charge for the loss?

Where a hazardous avocation sits on a file, does the house have the option of removing it with an exclusion rider naming the hazard instead of charging the avocation debits, and is that the house preference for technical rock climbing at about 19 days a year?
